signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Tension + Options Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 159.03, holding just below the 160.00 level which previously triggered intervention warnings. Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz following tanker assaults have introduced a geopolitical risk premium, yet the options market shows unusual complacency with IV at 7.2% sitting below HV30 at 8.6% (VRP -1.4%). The 25d risk reversal at -2.08 reflects a strong institutional demand for downside protection, contrasting with the relatively flat 52-week positioning percentile (pctl 73). While the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the structural anchor, the combination of sub-realized vol and extreme put skew suggests the market is underpricing the tail risk of a sudden carry unwind if geopolitical escalation forces a regime shift. Price remains above the SMA200 at 158.21, which serves as the primary technical floor for the carry trade. Trade bias: Neutral/Short USD/JPY; intervention risk and geopolitical tension cap the upside near 160.00. Catalyst: Next high-impact US data release. Risk: De-escalation in the Middle East allows carry demand to re-test the 161.1 SMA50 resistance.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5909 is the primary expression of the week's dominant G10 bilateral theme, with NZD outperforming the basket by +0.698% while the USD lags at -0.455%. This 1.153% spread develops despite a -125bp carry disadvantage for the NZD relative to the Fed's 3.75% rate. The RBNZ remains in a hiking cycle at 2.5%, and the local ESI at +7.9 is significantly outperforming the USD ESI of -14.9, suggesting fundamental data is surprising to the topside in New Zealand while cooling in the US. Speculative positioning is currently at a 52-week extreme short (pctl 2, z -2.00), creating an asymmetric short-squeeze environment as price holds above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5849/0.5789/0.5835). This setup implies that the NZD outperformance has room to extend as crowded shorts are forced to cover. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD, targeting a squeeze toward 0.6000. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep. Risk: A shift to risk-off sentiment (VIX > 25) would likely favor the USD and halt the NZD outperformance.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + COT Extreme
signals.text: EUR/USD is testing the 1.1582 level, supported by fading Fed rate hike bets and a restrictive ECB stance. The options market is pricing in significant protection with an IV of 7.1% against a realized HV30 of 4.2%, resulting in a notable +2.9% volatility risk premium. This elevated VRP suggests that institutional players are paying up for tails despite the pair trading in a established range above its SMA20 at 1.1485. CFTC data shows leveraged funds are heavily net short (pctl 8, z -2.17), while retail sentiment is 66% short, showing an alignment that typically precedes a deeper short-covering rally if 1.1600 is breached. The ECB hiking bias remains a tailwind against the 'on hold' Fed, providing a fundamental catalyst for the current strength. Trade bias: Long EUR/USD; positioning extreme supports a trend extension. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 70% hike priced). Risk: EUR/USD fails to close above the SMA200 at 1.1633, inviting a retracement to the SMA50 at 1.1469.

signals.title: GBP/JPY — Retail Extreme + Volatility Skew
signals.text: GBP/JPY is trading at 215.53 with a substantial +275bp carry advantage favoring the GBP (BoE 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%). Retail sentiment has reached an extreme 89% short bias, attempting to fade the carry-driven uptrend. However, the options market is signaling caution with a strong put skew in EUR/JPY (RR -1.96) which often bleeds into GBP/JPY risk appetite during JPY-centric moves. BoJ holds at 1.0%. While the carry remains the dominant driver, the retail extreme suggests a potential liquidity vacuum if the trend continues, though the high vol premium in GBP/USD (+5.0% VRP) indicates a cautious institutional backdrop. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/JPY; carry-supportive while retail remains trapped in shorts. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: Sudden BoJ hawkishness or intervention headline forces a retail-unwind-led reversal.
